correct.evidence: All 36 requests match hand counts (2026-11-30, 2026-07-03, 2026-06-22, 2020-06-19, 2021-06-18, 2026-12-23, 2028-01-03, today + 260 business days 2027-10-12, cap boundary 2026-05-01 both ways). The allowlist-only tree answers both routes byte-identically to the server, with and without published files.

sourced.evidence: Holidays come from the pack's calendar.federal_holidays_law row in force on each day, Juneteenth from its quote. The new offset limits are marked in the contract as Duly's own, never a rule. engine_literals passes.

never_assumes.evidence: A day with no holiday row gives holidays_not_known and the rest of the body is answered; a planning base or planning cap makes the answer planning; a base or result outside 1950-01-01..2099-12-31 gives outside_readable_dates.

inside_the_boundary.evidence: The new strings are missing reasons and contract descriptions; none addresses the student or says what to do. Copy lint is clean; drafts unchanged and still unapproved.

secure.evidence: days 1e9 and months 1e6 are 422 by the new maxima; 0001-01-01 and 9999-12-31 give a reason, no OverflowError. A file outside update.schema.json is never served. One unparsable file in pipeline/published/ still makes GET /v1/updates a 500 (finding 2).

tested.evidence: Mutants M1, M2, M3, M7 caught, and own M3b, M3c, M8, M13, M14, M16 caught. The bundle test runs both routes from the allowlist alone. Only M17 survives, the dead route handler (finding 1); no test has an unparsable published file.

findings.title: The route's CalendarNotInForceError handler and NO_CALENDAR can no longer run
findings.input: 1985-12-30 + 3 business days; mutant M17 removing the except clause
findings.what_happens: engine/schedule.py:120 catches the error per request, so the answer is 200 with holidays_not_known and M17 passes every test. The dead handler and NO_CALENDAR (line 34) say the opposite of openapi's 'A request the engine cannot date is not a 422'. Delete both and the import.

findings.title: One unparsable published file makes GET /v1/updates a 500
findings.input: pipeline/published/ holding one valid unblocked update and one file containing '{not json'
findings.what_happens: json.loads raises before the schema check, so the route is a 500 and the valid update is not served. Treat a file that does not parse as one outside update.schema.json, with a test.

findings.title: A planning base capped to a rule item stays planning
findings.input: a base item with planning true, capped to a non-planning item
findings.what_happens: The answer is the cap's rule date marked planning. This follows the contract as of a3f7a7a; the founder may prefer the cap to decide.

findings.title: A litigated base's status is not on the answer
findings.what_happens: Only rule_ids are carried, as in the first review; a caller looks the status up.
